question.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-2,5⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,1,3⟩-⟨-3,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨5,1,1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =⟨3,-2,5⟩\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
